summary: This note is a clipped Wikipedia article on the function key, a programmable key on computer and terminal keyboards that can trigger operating system or application actions. It covers the history of function keys from early Flexowriter, HP and IBM terminals through IBM PC keyboards, the layouts used on various keyboards and machines, and how macOS and Windows/MS-DOS assign default actions to F-keys. Navigation, language links and maintenance banners were ignored.
one_line: Wikipedia article describing function keys: their history, keyboard layouts across machines, and default actions on macOS and Windows.
key_facts: A function key is a key on a computer or terminal keyboard that can be programmed to cause the operating system or an application program to perform certain actions, a form of soft key.
The Singer/Friden 2201 Flexowriter Programmatic, introduced in 1965, had a cluster of 13 function keys labeled F1 to F13.
The HP 9830A (1972) had a 5×2 grid of 10 function keys at top left.
The IBM 3277 (1972) had 12 programmed function (PF) keys in a 3×4 matrix at the right of the keyboard.
The original IBM PC keyboard (PC/XT, 1981) had 10 function keys (F1–F10) in a 2×5 matrix at the left of the keyboard.
The Model M keyboard ('Enhanced', 1984) replaced the PC/XT function key layout with 12 keys in 3 blocks of 4 at the top of the keyboard.
NEC's PC-8001, introduced in 1979, featured five function keys at the top of the keyboard.
The HP 2640 (1975) used screen-labeled function keys, placing the keys close to the screen where labels could be displayed.
Under MS-DOS, F3 copied words from the previous command to the current command prompt.
Under Windows, the F1 key gradually became universally associated with Help in most early Windows programs.
F5 is commonly used as a reload key in many web browsers, while F11 activates full screen or kiosk mode on most browsers.
Alt+F4 is commonly used to quit an application, while Ctrl+F4 will often close a portion of the application, such as a document or tab.
In the classic Mac OS, the function keys could be configured by the user with the Function Keys control panel to start a program or run an AppleScript.
On Boot Camp, function keys F13 to F15 are mapped to the corresponding IBM PC keys Print Screen, Scroll Lock and Pause.
As of 2016, Apple has replaced the individual function keys with the touchbar on certain models of MacBook Pro.
